signs.text: SOUTERRAIN. From about the 700s, Irish farming families dug stone-lined passages under their forts, to store food and perhaps to hide when raiders came. Thousands are known, and more turn up under ploughs.

text: The roof is a row of flat slabs, laid with great care, and the passage narrows until you have to turn sideways. Whoever dug it was not expecting company.
Under a flat stone, in a rag: a small bronze brooch, a copy of a great one from the 700s. Left by an earlier visitor with a sense of humour.
